comments.content: Asserting `'0'` *after* the click is unintuitive and easy to misread as a bug later on — it only makes sense knowing that legacy mode compiles the expression with `$.untrack` (coarse-grained legacy reactivity), so `get()` reading a `$state` signal never re-runs the text update. Also, since `'0'` is the initial value too, the test would still pass if the click handler never ran or the DOM update broke in some other way. Consider asserting the initial render explicitly and documenting intent.

Minor style inconsistencies with the rest of the repo's samples (these files are prettier-ignored, hence not auto-fixed): double quotes in the import, no spaces around the arrow function body (`()=>set()`), and no trailing newline at end of file. Other samples in this directory (e.g. `derived-unowned-10`, `event-attribute-import`) use single quotes.

Naming this helper module `test.svelte.js` is confusing — it reads like a vitest test file, while the actual test config lives in `_config.js`. Other rune-module helpers in this suite are named for their purpose (`state.svelte.js`, `util.svelte.js`, `theme.svelte.js`). Consider renaming (e.g. `state.svelte.js`) and updating the import in `main.svelte`.

This sample does not exercise the new `maybe_runes` fallback it is named after. The `runtime-runes` suite compiles every component with `runes: true` (`tests/runtime-runes/test.ts` calls `runtime_suite(true)`, and `common_setup` appends `runes` to the compile options right after `...config.compileOptions`), so `analysis.runes` is already `true` here and `maybe_runes` is never set. As a result this test passes even if the compiler change is reverted. To cover the ambiguous case, the component must be compiled with `runes` left `undefined` (e.g. a compiler/snapshot test that calls `compile` without the `runes` option), or the config needs a way to override the suite-forced `runes` value.

`module.scope.references` is a native `Map` (see `Scope.references = new Map()` in `scope.js`), so `keys()` returns a `MapIterator`. `MapIterator.prototype.some` is an iterator-helper method that only exists in Node 22+/modern engines, while this package declares `engines.node >= 18` and CI runs the full test suite on Node 18/20 — calling `.some` here will throw `TypeError: ...some is not a function` and crash the compiler. Note line 409 in this same file correctly wraps with `Array.from(...)` before calling `.some`. Since the intent is just a membership test, using `Map.has` is simpler and avoids the extra iteration.
